question: What does the 'Ctrl + V' shortcut key do?

options.text: It pastes the copied text or files.
It copies the selected text or files.
It cuts the selected text or files.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It pastes the copied text or files**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ctrl + V** is a widely used **keyboard shortcut** in operating systems such as Windows, macOS, and Linux, as well as software applications, to paste the previously copied or cut content.
 
• When you press **Ctrl + C**, the selected content (text, images, files) gets copied to the clipboard, a temporary storage area in your computer’s memory.
 
• Pressing **Ctrl + V** inserts the copied or cut content from the clipboard into the selected location, such as a document, text field, or folder.
 
• This shortcut is a part of a group of standard shortcuts that also include **Ctrl + C** for copy, **Ctrl + X** for cut, and **Ctrl + Z** for undo.</li&g
